title: GetDescendants()
summary: Returns an array of EVERY instance beneath this one — children, grandchildren, and deeper. The workhorse for whole-tree operations (and the thing hand-rolled recursion usually imitates).

reference.returns: Flat array of every descendant at any depth. Can be large on workspace-sized calls.

details.heading: Cost
details.body: The array is built on every call — calling GetDescendants() on workspace every frame is a performance hazard. Call once and cache, or use targeted queries (tags, GetChildren on known containers).

explanation.whatItIs: The full family tree in one array — no manual recursion needed.
explanation.whyItExists: 'Do something to everything under here' is a constant need: counting parts, finding all Sounds, tagging geometry.
whenToUse: Finding all instances of a class under a model
Building caches of what exists at a moment in time
whenNotToUse: Every frame — cache or use events (ChildAdded/DescendantAdded)
On huge trees when a tag or direct path would do
Repeatedly for the same question — restructure data instead
tips: Filter with IsA in the loop
DescendantAdded event for 'react to new things under here'
For known shapes, direct paths beat whole-tree scans
commonMistakes: GetDescendants on workspace in Heartbeat — framerate killer
Expecting the returned array to update as the tree changes
Scanning when CollectionService tags already answer the question

examples.title: Find every Sound under a model
examples.code:
local map = workspace.Map

local sounds = {}
for _, descendant in map:GetDescendants() do
    if descendant:IsA("Sound") then
        table.insert(sounds, descendant)
    end
end
print(`Map contains {#sounds} sounds`)

examples.title: React to new descendants
examples.code:
workspace.Map.DescendantAdded:Connect(function(instance)
    if instance:IsA("BasePart") then
        instance:SetAttribute("MapPart", true)
    end
end)
